142	class KeyProvider:
143	    """Abstract provider; concrete providers implement the five operations."""
144	
145	    provider_id = ""
146	    capabilities = {"algorithms": (), "operations": ()}
147	
148	    def configure(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
149	        """Bind any persistent state to the data directory (optional)."""
150	
151	    def generate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
152	        raise NotImplementedError
153	
154	    def rotate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
155	        raise NotImplementedError
156	
157	    def import_material(
158	        self,
159	        algorithm: str,
160	        public_key: Optional[str],
161	        material: str,
162	    ) -> MaterialTriple:
163	        raise NotImplementedError
164	
165	    def export_material(self, handle: str) -> ExportedMaterial:
166	        raise NotImplementedError
167	
168	    def delete(self, handle: str) -> None:
169	        raise NotImplementedError
170	
171	    def supports(self, algorithm: str, operation: str) -> bool:
172	        caps = getattr(self, "capabilities", {}) or {}
173	        return (
174	            algorithm in caps.get("algorithms", ())
175	            and operation in caps.get("operations", ())
176	        )
177	
178	
179	def _validate_external(obj) -> None:
180	    """Check a factory-built object satisfies the provider contract."""
181	    provider_id = getattr(obj, "provider_id", None)
182	    if not isinstance(provider_id, str) or not provider_id:
183	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
184	            "provider factory returned an object without a non-empty provider_id"
185	        )
186	    caps = getattr(obj, "capabilities", None)
187	    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
188	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
189	            "provider %r has no capabilities mapping" % provider_id
190	        )
191	    algorithms = caps.get("algorithms")
192	    operations = caps.get("operations")
193	    if not isinstance(algorithms, (list, tuple)) or not isinstance(
194	        operations, (list, tuple)
195	    ):
196	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
197	            "provider %r capabilities must list algorithms and operations"
198	            % provider_id
199	        )
200	    missing = [a for a in SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS if a not in algorithms]
201	    if missing:
202	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
203	            "provider %r lacks required algorithms: %s"
204	            % (provider_id, ", ".join(missing))
205	        )
206	    missing_ops = [op for op in OPERATIONS if op not in operations]
207	    if missing_ops:
208	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
209	            "provider %r lacks required operations: %s"
210	            % (provider_id, ", ".join(missing_ops))
211	        )
212	    for name in OPERATIONS:
213	        if not callable(getattr(obj, name, None)):
214	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
215	                "provider %r is missing a callable %s() operation"
216	                % (provider_id, name)
217	            )
218	    configure = getattr(obj, "configure", None)
219	    if configure is not None and not callable(configure):
220	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
221	            "provider %r has a non-callable configure attribute" % provider_id
222	        )
223	
224	
225	class _SafeProvider:
226	    """Adapter around an external provider enforcing the error contract.
227	
228	    ProviderError subtypes pass through unchanged; any other exception the
229	    external module raises is normalized to ProviderUnavailable so a backend
230	    fault always surfaces as 503 and never as a 500 or a fallback.
231	    """
232	
233	    def __init__(self, inner) -> None:
234	        self._inner = inner
235	        self.provider_id = inner.provider_id
236	        self.capabilities = inner.capabilities
237	
238	    def configure(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
239	        try:
240	            configure = getattr(self._inner, "configure", None)
241	            if configure is not None:
242	                configure(data_dir)
243	        except ProviderError:
244	            raise
245	        except Exception as exc:
246	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
247	                "provider %r failed to initialize" % self.provider_id
248	            ) from exc
249	
250	    def _call(self, name: str, *args):
251	        method = getattr(self._inner, name)
252	        try:
253	            return method(*args)
254	        except ProviderError:
255	            raise
256	        except Exception as exc:
257	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
258	                "provider %r operation %s failed" % (self.provider_id, name)
259	            ) from exc
260	
261	    def generate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
262	        return _require_triple(self._call("generate", algorithm), "generate")
263	
264	    def rotate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
265	        return _require_triple(self._call("rotate", algorithm), "rotate")
266	
267	    def import_material(self, algorithm, public_key, material) -> MaterialTriple:
268	        return _require_triple(
269	            self._call("import_material", algorithm, public_key, material),
270	            "import_material",
271	        )
272	
273	    def export_material(self, handle: str) -> ExportedMaterial:
274	        result = self._call("export_material", handle)
275	        if not isinstance(result, dict):
276	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
277	                "provider returned a non-object from export_material"
278	            )
279	        material = result.get("encrypted_material")
280	        if not isinstance(material, str) or not material:
281	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
282	                "provider returned empty encrypted_material from export_material"
283	            )
284	        public_key = result.get("public_key")
285	        if public_key is not None and not isinstance(public_key, str):
286	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
287	                "provider returned an invalid public_key from export_material"
288	            )
289	        return ExportedMaterial(
290	            public_key=public_key, encrypted_material=material
291	        )
292	
293	    def delete(self, handle: str) -> None:
294	        # Idempotent by contract; even so, a backend fault on delete is a 503
295	        # (the caller may retry, and delete must remain idempotent).
296	        self._call("delete", handle)
297	
298	
299	class LocalProvider(KeyProvider):
300	    """Built-in software provider.
301	
302	    Raw material never lands in a key file: each generated/imported key is
303	    wrapped with AES-256-GCM under a data-encryption key kept in
304	    ``local.dek`` (0600), and only the wrapped blob plus an opaque handle is
305	    persisted. A small registry (``local-registry.json``, 0600) maps each
306	    handle to its algorithm and wrapped blob, so ``export_material(handle)``
307	    can re-derive the raw material and ``delete`` stays idempotent. The
308	    registry stores only DEK-wrapped material, never plaintext.
309	    """
310	
311	    provider_id = LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID
312	    capabilities = {
313	        "algorithms": tuple(SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS),
314	        "operations": OPERATIONS,
315	    }
316	
317	    def __init__(self) -> None:
318	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
319	        self._data_dir: Optional[str] = None
320	        self._dek: Optional[bytes] = None
321	        self._registry: dict = {}
322	        self._configured = False
323	
324	    # -- state -------------------------------------------------------------
325	    def configure(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
326	        with self._lock:
327	            if self._configured and self._data_dir == data_dir:
328	                return
329	            os.makedirs(data_dir, exist_ok=True)
330	            self._data_dir = data_dir
331	            self._dek = self._load_or_create_dek(data_dir)
332	            self._registry = self._load_registry(data_dir)
333	            self._configured = True
334	
335	    @staticmethod
336	    def _load_or_create_dek(data_dir: str) -> bytes:
337	        path = os.path.join(data_dir, _DEK_NAME)
338	        try:
339	            with open(path, "rb") as fh:
340	                dek = fh.read()
341	            if len(dek) == 32:
342	                return dek
343	        except FileNotFoundError:
344	            pass
345	        except OSError as exc:
346	            raise ProviderUnavailable("cannot read local DEK: %s" % exc) from exc
347	        dek = os.urandom(32)
348	        try:
349	            fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
350	            try:
351	                os.write(fd, dek)
352	                os.fsync(fd)
353	            finally:
354	                os.close(fd)
355	        except FileExistsError:
356	            with open(path, "rb") as fh:
357	                dek = fh.read()
358	        except OSError as exc:
359	            raise ProviderUnavailable("cannot write local DEK: %s" % exc) from exc
360	        if len(dek) != 32:
361	            raise ProviderUnavailable("local DEK file is corrupt")
362	        return dek
363	
364	    @staticmethod
365	    def _load_registry(data_dir: str) -> dict:
366	        path = os.path.join(data_dir, _REGISTRY_NAME)
367	        try:
368	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
369	                data = json.load(fh)
370	        except FileNotFoundError:
371	            return {}
372	        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
373	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
374	                "cannot read local handle registry: %s" % exc
375	            ) from exc
376	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
377	            raise ProviderUnavailable("local handle registry is corrupt")
378	        return data
379	
380	    def _persist_registry_locked(self) -> None:
381	        path = os.path.join(self._data_dir, _REGISTRY_NAME)
382	        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=self._data_dir, suffix=".tmp")
383	        try:
384	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
385	                json.dump(self._registry, fh)
386	                fh.flush()
387	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
388	            os.chmod(tmp_path, 0o600)
389	            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
390	        except BaseException:
391	            try:
392	                os.unlink(tmp_path)
393	            except OSError:
394	                pass
395	            raise
396	
397	    def _require_configured(self) -> None:
398	        if not self._configured:
399	            raise ProviderUnavailable("local provider is not configured")
400	
401	    # -- wrapping ----------------------------------------------------------
402	    def _wrap_locked(self, raw_material: str) -> str:
403	        nonce = os.urandom(_NONCE_LEN)
404	        ct = AESGCM(self._dek).encrypt(
405	            nonce, raw_material.encode("utf-8"), None
406	        )
407	        return _WRAP_PREFIX + _b64e(nonce) + "." + _b64e(ct)
408	
409	    def _unwrap_locked(self, blob: str) -> str:
410	        if not isinstance(blob, str) or not blob.startswith(_WRAP_PREFIX):
411	            raise ProviderUnavailable("stored material is not a local blob")
412	        try:
413	            nonce_b, ct_b = blob[len(_WRAP_PREFIX):].split(".", 1)
414	            nonce = _b64d(nonce_b)
415	            ct = _b64d(ct_b)
416	            raw = AESGCM(self._dek).decrypt(nonce, ct, None)
417	            return raw.decode("utf-8")
418	        except Exception as exc:
419	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
420	                "cannot unwrap local material"
421	            ) from exc
422	
423	    # -- material validation ----------------------------------------------
424	    @staticmethod
425	    def _validate_material(
426	        algorithm: str, public_key, material
427	    ):
428	        """Validate raw (legacy-shaped) material for an algorithm.
429	
430	        AES material is base64 of exactly 32 bytes and has no public part;
431	        RSA material is a PEM private key of exactly 2048 bits, and the
432	        supplied public key (when present) must match it. Returns the parsed
433	        RSA private key (None for AES).
434	        """
435	        if not isinstance(material, str) or not material:
436	            raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
437	                "field encrypted_material must be a non-empty string"
438	            )
439	        if algorithm == "AES256":
440	            if public_key is not None:
441	                raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
442	                    "field public_key must be null for AES256"
443	                )
444	            try:
445	                raw = base64.b64decode(material, validate=True)
446	            except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
447	                raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
448	                    "field encrypted_material must be valid base64 for AES256"
449	                ) from exc
450	            if len(raw) != 32:
451	                raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
452	                    "field encrypted_material must decode to 32 bytes for AES256"
453	                )
454	            return None
455	        if algorithm == "RSA2048":
456	            try:
457	                private_key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(
458	                    material.encode("utf-8"), password=None
459	                )
460	            except (ValueError, TypeError, UnsupportedAlgorithm) as exc:
461	                raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
462	                    "field encrypted_material must be a PEM private key for RSA2048"
463	                ) from exc
464	            if not isinstance(private_key, rsa.RSAPrivateKey) or (
465	                private_key.key_size != 2048
466	            ):
467	                raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
468	                    "field encrypted_material must be a 2048-bit RSA private key"
469	                )
470	            if public_key is not None:
471	                if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not public_key:
472	                    raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
473	                        "field public_key must be a PEM string for RSA2048"
474	                    )
475	                try:
476	                    supplied = serialization.load_pem_public_key(
477	                        public_key.encode("utf-8")
478	                    )
479	                    if not isinstance(supplied, rsa.RSAPublicKey):
480	                        raise ValueError("not an RSA public key")
481	                except (ValueError, TypeError, UnsupportedAlgorithm) as exc:
482	                    raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
483	                        "field public_key must be a PEM RSA public key"
484	                    ) from exc
485	                expected = private_key.public_key().public_bytes(
486	                    encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,
487	                    format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,
488	                )
489	                actual = supplied.public_bytes(
490	                    encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,
491	                    format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,
492	                )
493	                if expected != actual:
494	                    raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
495	                        "field public_key does not match the private key"
496	                    )
497	            return private_key
498	        raise ProviderInvalidMaterial(
499	            "unsupported value for field algorithm: %r (supported: %s)"
500	            % (algorithm, ", ".join(SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS))
501	        )
502	
503	    @staticmethod
504	    def _public_pem(private_key) -> str:
505	        return private_key.public_key().public_bytes(
506	            encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
507	            format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,
508	        ).decode("ascii")
509	
510	    def _adopt(
511	        self,
512	        algorithm: str,
513	        public_key,
514	        raw_material: str,
515	    ) -> MaterialTriple:
516	        """Validate raw material, wrap it under the DEK, mint a handle."""
517	        self._require_configured()
518	        private_key = self._validate_material(algorithm, public_key, raw_material)
519	        if algorithm == "RSA2048" and public_key is None:
520	            public_key = self._public_pem(private_key)
521	        handle = uuid.uuid4().hex
522	        with self._lock:
523	            wrapped = self._wrap_locked(raw_material)
524	            self._registry[handle] = {
525	                "algorithm": algorithm,
526	                "wrapped": wrapped,
527	            }
528	            self._persist_registry_locked()
529	        return MaterialTriple(
530	            handle=handle,
531	            public_key=public_key,
532	            encrypted_material=wrapped,
533	        )
534	
535	    # -- KeyProvider operations -------------------------------------------
536	    def generate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
537	        generated = generate_key(algorithm)
538	        return self._adopt(
539	            algorithm, generated.public_material, generated.private_material
540	        )
541	
542	    def rotate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
543	        # A rotated version is brand-new material owned by the same provider.
544	        return self.generate(algorithm)
545	
546	    def import_material(
547	        self,
548	        algorithm: str,
549	        public_key,
550	        material: str,
551	    ) -> MaterialTriple:
552	        return self._adopt(algorithm, public_key, material)
553	
554	    def export_material(self, handle: str) -> ExportedMaterial:
555	        """Return the raw bundle-shaped material for a registered handle.
556	
557	        The registry keeps the DEK-wrapped blob, which is unwrapped here. The
558	        returned material is only ever sealed inside a passphrase-encrypted
559	        export bundle; an unknown handle is ProviderUnavailable.
560	        """
561	        self._require_configured()
562	        if not isinstance(handle, str) or not handle:
563	            raise ProviderUnavailable("export_material requires a handle")
564	        with self._lock:
565	            meta = self._registry.get(handle)
566	            if meta is None:
567	                raise ProviderUnavailable("unknown handle")
568	            algorithm = meta.get("algorithm")
569	            blob = meta.get("wrapped")
570	            try:
571	                raw = self._unwrap_locked(blob)
572	            except ProviderUnavailable:
573	                raise
574	        if algorithm == "AES256":
575	            return ExportedMaterial(public_key=None, encrypted_material=raw)
576	        try:
577	            private_key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(
578	                raw.encode("utf-8"), password=None
579	            )
580	        except (ValueError, TypeError, UnsupportedAlgorithm) as exc:
581	            raise ProviderUnavailable("stored local material is corrupt") from exc
582	        return ExportedMaterial(
583	            public_key=self._public_pem(private_key),
584	            encrypted_material=raw,
585	        )
586	
587	    def delete(self, handle: str) -> None:
588	        """Drop a handle from the registry. Idempotent and never fails 404."""
589	        self._require_configured()
590	        with self._lock:
591	            if handle in self._registry:
592	                del self._registry[handle]
593	                self._persist_registry_locked()
594

        path = self._path_for(key_id)
        with self._key_lock(key_id), self._file_lock(key_id):

            # A version is rotated on the provider that owns the record;

            previous = record.to_json()

The three mutating endpoints

* ``POST /v1/keys/{key_id}/rotate``
* ``POST /v1/keys/import``
* ``POST /v1/restore``

accept an ``Idempotency-Key`` header (CLI: ``--idempotency-key``). A key is
1-128 ASCII characters from ``[A-Za-z0-9._~-]``; a missing, empty, duplicated
or illegal header is a ``400`` (CLI exit ``2``) with no side effects.

A binding is the triple ``(tenant_id, operator, idempotency_key)``. The first
request mints a UUID4 ``operation_id`` (also used as the committing audit
``event_id``), records a ``pending`` operation, and is the only request that
submits. A retry with the same binding and the same canonicalized body reuses
the stored status code, response and audit event; the same binding with a
different body (or path) answers ``409`` naming the existing operation_id.
Concurrent requests for one binding serialize; a request that waits more than
five seconds on the binding lock answers ``503`` ``timed_out`` without
writing keys, audit events or provider handles.

Operation state: ``pending`` / ``succeeded`` / ``failed`` / ``conflict`` /
``timed_out``. Every response produced for a bound operation carries its
``operation_id``; error bodies contain only ``error`` and ``operation_id``.

``GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}`` is scoped to one tenant and operator:
``200`` gives ``operation_id``, ``tenant_id``, ``status``, ``http_status`` and
``response`` (the last two null while pending); an unknown id or another
tenant's (or operator's) operation answers ``404``.

Crash recovery keys on operation_id == event_id: at startup each leftover
pending operation is finalized from the ledger/outbox state, and half-written
files and provider handles are reaped by the existing outbox/provision
recovery. The semantics are identical over HTTP and the CLI.

import tempfile

STATUS_CONFLICT = "conflict"

"""Idempotent operations for key rotate / import / tenant restore.

The three mutating endpoints

* ``POST /v1/keys/{key_id}/rotate``
* ``POST /v1/keys/import``
* ``POST /v1/restore``

accept an ``Idempotency-Key`` header (CLI: ``--idempotency-key``). A key is
1-128 ASCII characters from ``[A-Za-z0-9._~-]``; a missing, empty, duplicated
or illegal header is a ``400`` (CLI exit ``2``) with no side effects.

A binding is the triple ``(tenant_id, operator, idempotency_key)``. The first
request mints a UUID4 ``operation_id`` (also used as the committing audit
``event_id``), records a ``pending`` operation, and is the only request that
submits. A retry with the same binding and the same canonicalized body reuses
the stored status code, response and audit event; the same binding with a
different body (or path) answers ``409`` naming the existing operation_id.
Concurrent requests for one binding serialize; a request that waits more than
five seconds on the binding lock answers ``503`` ``timed_out`` without
writing keys, audit events or provider handles.

Operation state: ``pending`` / ``succeeded`` / ``failed`` / ``conflict`` /
``timed_out``. Every response produced for a bound operation carries its
``operation_id``; error bodies contain only ``error`` and ``operation_id``.

``GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}`` is scoped to one tenant and operator:
``200`` gives ``operation_id``, ``tenant_id``, ``status``, ``http_status`` and
``response`` (the last two null while pending); an unknown id or another
tenant's (or operator's) operation answers ``404``.

Crash recovery keys on operation_id == event_id: at startup each leftover
pending operation is finalized from the ledger/outbox state, and half-written
files and provider handles are reaped by the existing outbox/provision
recovery. The semantics are identical over HTTP and the CLI.
"""

import os
import tempfile
import threading
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

try:  # fcntl is POSIX-only; binding locks degrade to in-process elsewhere.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
    fcntl = None

# Endpoints covered by idempotency, and their logical (canonical) paths. The
# CLI synthesizes the same path strings so HTTP and CLI share one fingerprint
# space.
OP_ROTATE = "rotate"
OP_IMPORT = "import"
OP_RESTORE = "restore"

ROTATE_PATH = "/v1/keys/%s/rotate"
IMPORT_PATH = "/v1/keys/import"
RESTORE_PATH = "/v1/restore"

#: Operation states.
STATUS_PENDING = "pending"
STATUS_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
STATUS_FAILED = "failed"
STATUS_CONFLICT = "conflict"
STATUS_TIMED_OUT = "timed_out"
TERMINAL_STATES = (STATUS_SUCCEEDED, STATUS_FAILED)

#: Wait bound for a binding lock, after which the waiter answers timed_out.
LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 5.0

class IdempotencyKeyError(ValueError):
    """The Idempotency-Key header/argument is missing, empty or illegal.

    Surfaced as HTTP ``400`` / CLI exit ``2`` before any operation state is
    created (no side effects).
    """


class BindingConflict(Exception):
    """Same (tenant, operator, key) binding is reused with another request.

    The conflicting request answers ``409`` naming the *existing*
    operation_id; no new operation is created and the existing one is not
    modified.
    """

    def __init__(self, existing_operation_id: str) -> None:
        super().__init__("idempotency key is bound to a different request")
        self.existing_operation_id = existing_operation_id


class BindingTimeout(Exception):
    """Waiting on a binding lock took longer than ``LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS``.

    Nothing is written by the waiter. ``operation_id`` is the in-flight
    binding's operation when its record was already observable.
    """

    def __init__(self, operation_id: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        super().__init__("timed out waiting for idempotent operation lock")
        self.operation_id = operation_id

class OperationStore:
    """Persistent idempotent-operation records and their execution facade."""

    def __init__(self, data_dir: str, store, policy_store, coordinator) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    # -- entry points used by the HTTP handlers and the CLI ---------------
    def run_rotate(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: str,
        operator: str,
        idempotency_key: str,
        key_id: str,
        payload: dict,
    ) -> OperationRecord:
        """Run (or replay) an idempotent rotate."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def run_import(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: str,
        operator: str,
        idempotency_key: str,
        payload: dict,
    ) -> OperationRecord:
        """Run (or replay) an idempotent single-key import."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def run_restore(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: str,
        operator: str,
        idempotency_key: str,
        payload: dict,
    ) -> OperationRecord:
        """Run (or replay) an idempotent tenant restore."""
        raise NotImplementedError

        self,
        operation_id: str,
        tenant_id: str,
        operator: str,

        """Return an operation owned by this tenant AND operator, else None."""
        raise NotImplementedError

def is_valid_idempotency_key(value) -> bool:
    """True for 1-128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9._~-] (ASCII only)."""
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not 1 <= len(value) <= 128:
        return False
    try:
        value.encode("ascii")
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        return False
    for ch in value:
        if not (
            "a" <= ch <= "z"
            or "A" <= ch <= "Z"
            or "0" <= ch <= "9"
            or ch in "._~-"
        ):
            return False
    return True

    """SHA-256 over the canonical path plus canonicalized JSON body.

    The body is re-serialized with sorted keys and compact separators, so two
    requests differing only in JSON whitespace or key order are the same

    body = json.dumps(
        payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
    )
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    digest.update(path.encode("utf-8"))
    digest.update(b"\n")
    digest.update(body.encode("utf-8"))
    return digest.hexdigest()

    """One idempotent operation, persisted as a single 0600 JSON file."""

    operation_id: str
    idempotency_key: str

    created_at: Optional[str] = None
    updated_at: Optional[str] = None

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        """Serialize to a plain dict suitable for JSON storage."""
        return {
            "version": 1,
            "operation_id": self.operation_id,
            "idempotency_key": self.idempotency_key,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "operator": self.operator,
            "path": self.path,
            "request_fingerprint": self.request_fingerprint,
            "status": self.status,
            "http_status": self.http_status,
            "response": self.response,
            "intent": self.intent,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "updated_at": self.updated_at,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "OperationRecord":
        return cls(
            operation_id=data["operation_id"],
            idempotency_key=data["idempotency_key"],
            tenant_id=data["tenant_id"],
            operator=data["operator"],
            path=data["path"],
            request_fingerprint=data["request_fingerprint"],
            status=data.get("status", STATUS_PENDING),
            http_status=data.get("http_status"),
            response=data.get("response"),
            intent=data.get("intent"),
            created_at=data.get("created_at"),
            updated_at=data.get("updated_at"),
        )

    def to_status_response(self) -> dict:
        """Body of GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}.

        http_status and response are both null while the operation is
        pending; a terminal operation carries the exact status code and the
        exact response body a retry would receive.
        """
        if self.status == STATUS_PENDING:
            http_status = None
            response = None
        else:
            http_status = self.http_status
            response = self.response
        return {
            "operation_id": self.operation_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "status": self.status,
            "http_status": http_status,
            "response": response,
        }

    @property
    def terminal(self) -> bool:
        return self.status in (
            STATUS_SUCCEEDED,
            STATUS_FAILED,
            STATUS_CONFLICT,
            STATUS_TIMED_OUT,
        )

    """An executor-raised terminal failure of a bound operation.

    updated_at: Optional[str] = None

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        """Serialize to a plain dict suitable for JSON storage."""
        return {
            "version": 1,
            "operation_id": self.operation_id,
            "idempotency_key": self.idempotency_key,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "operator": self.operator,
            "path": self.path,
            "request_fingerprint": self.request_fingerprint,
            "status": self.status,
            "http_status": self.http_status,
            "response": self.response,
            "intent": self.intent,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "updated_at": self.updated_at,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "OperationRecord":
        return cls(
            operation_id=data["operation_id"],
            idempotency_key=data["idempotency_key"],
            tenant_id=data["tenant_id"],
            operator=data["operator"],
            path=data["path"],
            request_fingerprint=data["request_fingerprint"],
            status=data.get("status", STATUS_PENDING),
            http_status=data.get("http_status"),
            response=data.get("response"),
            intent=data.get("intent"),
            created_at=data.get("created_at"),
            updated_at=data.get("updated_at"),
        )

    def to_status_response(self) -> dict:
        """Body of GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}.

        http_status and response are both null while the operation is
        pending; a terminal operation carries the exact status code and the
        exact response body a retry would receive.
        """
        if self.status == STATUS_PENDING:
            http_status = None
            response = None
        else:
            http_status = self.http_status
            response = self.response
        return {
            "operation_id": self.operation_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "status": self.status,
            "http_status": http_status,
            "response": response,
        }

    @property
    def terminal(self) -> bool:
        return self.status in (
            STATUS_SUCCEEDED,
            STATUS_FAILED,
            STATUS_CONFLICT,
            STATUS_TIMED_OUT,
        )

"""Idempotent operations for key rotate / import / tenant restore.

The three mutating endpoints

* ``POST /v1/keys/{key_id}/rotate``
* ``POST /v1/keys/import``
* ``POST /v1/restore``

accept an ``Idempotency-Key`` header (CLI: ``--idempotency-key``). A key is
1-128 ASCII characters from ``[A-Za-z0-9._~-]``; a missing, empty, duplicated
or illegal header is a ``400`` (CLI exit ``2``) with no side effects.

A binding is the triple ``(tenant_id, operator, idempotency_key)``. The first
request mints a UUID4 ``operation_id`` (also used as the committing audit
``event_id``), records a ``pending`` operation, and is the only request that
submits. A retry with the same binding and the same canonicalized body reuses
the stored status code, response and audit event; the same binding with a
different body (or path) answers ``409`` naming the existing operation_id.
Concurrent requests for one binding serialize; a request that waits more than
five seconds on the binding lock answers ``503`` ``timed_out`` without
writing keys, audit events or provider handles.

Operation state: ``pending`` / ``succeeded`` / ``failed`` / ``conflict`` /
``timed_out``. Every response produced for a bound operation carries its
``operation_id``; error bodies contain only ``error`` and ``operation_id``.

``GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}`` is scoped to one tenant and operator:
``200`` gives ``operation_id``, ``tenant_id``, ``status``, ``http_status`` and
``response`` (the last two null while pending); an unknown id or another
tenant's (or operator's) operation answers ``404``.

Crash recovery keys on operation_id == event_id: at startup each leftover
pending operation is finalized from the ledger/outbox state, and half-written
files and provider handles are reaped by the existing outbox/provision
recovery. The semantics are identical over HTTP and the CLI.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Optional

from . import audit as audit_mod
from . import keybundle
from . import tenantbundle
from .audit import LedgerError
from .crypto import SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS
from .provider import ProviderInvalidMaterial, ProviderUnavailable
from .restore import (

    RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT,
)
from .store import IMPORT_CONFLICT, is_valid_key_id

try:  # fcntl is POSIX-only; binding locks degrade to in-process elsewhere.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms

# Endpoints covered by idempotency, and their logical (canonical) paths. The

OP_ROTATE = "rotate"
OP_IMPORT = "import"
OP_RESTORE = "restore"

ROTATE_PATH = "/v1/keys/%s/rotate"
IMPORT_PATH = "/v1/keys/import"
RESTORE_PATH = "/v1/restore"

#: Operation states.
STATUS_PENDING = "pending"
STATUS_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
STATUS_FAILED = "failed"
STATUS_CONFLICT = "conflict"
STATUS_TIMED_OUT = "timed_out"
TERMINAL_STATES = (STATUS_SUCCEEDED, STATUS_FAILED)

#: Wait bound for a binding lock, after which the waiter answers timed_out.
LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 5.0

class IdempotencyKeyError(ValueError):
    """The Idempotency-Key header/argument is missing, empty or illegal.

    Surfaced as HTTP ``400`` / CLI exit ``2`` before any operation state is
    created (no side effects).
    """


class BindingConflict(Exception):
    """Same (tenant, operator, key) binding is reused with another request.

    The conflicting request answers ``409`` naming the *existing*
    operation_id; no new operation is created and the existing one is not
    modified.
    """

    def __init__(self, existing_operation_id: str) -> None:
        super().__init__("idempotency key is bound to a different request")
        self.existing_operation_id = existing_operation_id


class BindingTimeout(Exception):
    """Waiting on a binding lock took longer than ``LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS``.

    Nothing is written by the waiter. ``operation_id`` is the in-flight
    binding's operation when its record was already observable.
    """

    def __init__(self, operation_id: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        super().__init__("timed out waiting for idempotent operation lock")
        self.operation_id = operation_id


def is_valid_idempotency_key(value) -> bool:
    """True for 1-128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9._~-] (ASCII only)."""
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not 1 <= len(value) <= 128:
        return False
    try:
        value.encode("ascii")
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        return False
    for ch in value:
        if not (
            "a" <= ch <= "z"
            or "A" <= ch <= "Z"
            or "0" <= ch <= "9"
            or ch in "._~-"
        ):
            return False
    return True


def canonical_fingerprint(path: str, payload: dict) -> str:
    """SHA-256 over the canonical path plus canonicalized JSON body.

    The body is re-serialized with sorted keys and compact separators, so two
    requests differing only in JSON whitespace or key order are the same
    request; any field difference is a different request.
    """
    body = json.dumps(
        payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
    )
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    digest.update(path.encode("utf-8"))
    digest.update(b"\n")
    digest.update(body.encode("utf-8"))
    return digest.hexdigest()

# -- crash recovery ----------------------------------------------------
    def recover_pending(self) -> None:
        """Finalize leftover pending operations after a restart.

        The key/outbox stores have already resolved pending markers and
        reaped handles keyed by the same ids (operation_id == event_id ==
        journal id). A pinned success event in the ledger commits the
        operation; its response is rebuilt from durable state (and the
        pre-execution ``intent`` carried in the record). A pending operation
        whose event never reached the ledger is left pending: it changed
        nothing, and the next same-binding retry (which carries the body
        again) re-executes it under the same operation_id.
        """
        try:
            names = os.listdir(self.dir_path)
        except OSError:
            return
        for name in names:
            if not name.endswith(".json"):
                continue
            operation_id = name[:-5]
            record = self._read_op(operation_id)
            if record is None or record.status != STATUS_PENDING:
                continue
            try:
                event = self.audit.get_event(operation_id)
            except LedgerError:
                # The ledger cannot be read right now; leave it pending for a
                # later open or a live same-binding request to resolve.
                continue
            if event is not None and event.outcome == audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS:
                try:
                    self._rebuild_success(record, event)
                except _RebuildUnavailable:
                    continue
            elif event is not None:
                # A rejected event is always staged *after* its terminal
                # operation record, so a pending record here means the
                # ledger holds a stray line: mark the operation failed
                # rather than re-running anything.
                self._terminalize(
                    record, 500,
                    "operation interrupted before completion",
                    STATUS_FAILED,
                )
            # No event: leave pending for the next live retry.

    def _resume_pending(self, record: OperationRecord) -> bool:
        """Resolve a pending record from the ledger before a live retry.

        True when the record was finalized (committed success); False when
        its event is absent, i.e. nothing committed and the caller should
        re-execute under the same operation_id.
        """
        event = self.audit.get_event(record.operation_id)
        if event is None:
            return False
        if event.outcome == audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS:
            self._rebuild_success(record, event)
            return True
        self._terminalize(
            record, 500, "operation interrupted before completion",
            STATUS_FAILED,
        )
        return True

    # -- terminal states ---------------------------------------------------
    def _terminalize(
        self,
        record: OperationRecord,
        http_status: int,
        message: Optional[str],
        op_status: str,
        response: Optional[dict] = None,
    ) -> None:
        if response is None:
            response = {
                "error": message,
                "operation_id": record.operation_id,
            }
        record.status = op_status
        record.http_status = http_status
        record.response = response
        self._persist(record)

    def _succeed(
        self, record: OperationRecord, http_status: int, body: dict
    ) -> None:
        response = dict(body)
        response["operation_id"] = record.operation_id
        self._terminalize(
            record, http_status, None, STATUS_SUCCEEDED, response=response
        )

    def _reject(
        self,
        record: OperationRecord,
        http_status: int,
        message: str,
        op_status: str = STATUS_FAILED,
        *,
        tenant_id=None,
        key_id=None,
        action=None,
        invisible: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Stage a terminal error response, then append the pinned event.

        The terminal record lands first, so a crash either before or after
        the ledger append leaves a replayable result; the pinned event id
        makes the append idempotent. If the ledger append itself fails the
        request is a 500 (the staged 4xx is overwritten).
        """
        self._terminalize(record, http_status, message, op_status)
        try:
            if invisible:
                self.store.audit_conflict(event_id=record.operation_id)
            elif action is not None:
                self.store.audit_attempt(
                    tenant_id, key_id, action, audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
                    event_id=record.operation_id,
                )
        except LedgerError as exc:
            message500 = "audit ledger failure: %s" % exc
            self._terminalize(
                record, 500, message500, STATUS_FAILED
            )
            raise _ExecError(500, message500, STATUS_FAILED)
        raise _ExecError(http_status, message, op_status)

        def _get_operation(self, operation_id: str, parts, operator: str) -> None:
            """GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}.

            Requires a single tenant (one X-Tenant-Id header or one
            tenant_id parameter, never both) and the single operator that
            created the operation. An unknown id, another tenant's or
            another operator's operation all answer 404 so existence never

            if tenant_id is None:

            record = operations.get_operation(

            )
            if record is None:
                self._send_json(404, {"error": "operation not found"})
                return
            self._send_json(200, record.to_status_response())

def serve(host: str, port: int, data_dir: str) -> None:

"""End-to-end checks for idempotent rotate/import/restore."""
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
import uuid
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer

from keymgr.audit import AuditLog
from keymgr import operations as ops_mod
from keymgr.operations import (
    OperationStore, OperationRecord, STATUS_SUCCEEDED, STATUS_FAILED,
    STATUS_CONFLICT, STATUS_PENDING,
)
from keymgr.policy import PolicyStore
from keymgr import restore as restore_mod
from keymgr.server import make_handler
from keymgr.store import KeyStore
from keymgr.crypto import SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS

ROOT = "/tmp/keymgr_idem_test"
PORT = 18099

failures = []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    if cond:
        print("PASS", name)
    else:
        print("FAIL", name, detail)
        failures.append(name)


def http(method, path, body=None, headers=None, raw=None):
    url = "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (PORT, path)
    data = raw if raw is not None else (
        json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    )
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
    req.add_header("X-Operator-Id", "alice")
    for k, v in (headers or {}).items():
        if k.lower() == "x-operator-id":
            req.remove_header("X-Operator-Id") if False else None
        req.add_header(k, v)
    # urllib dedups headers by combining; to truly duplicate a header use low-level
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, json.loads(e.read())


def http_dup_header(path, header, values, body):
    """Send a request with a genuinely duplicated header via raw socket."""
    import http.client
    conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", PORT, timeout=10)
    conn.putrequest("POST", path)
    conn.putheader("Content-Type", "application/json")
    raw = json.dumps(body).encode()
    conn.putheader("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
    conn.putheader("X-Operator-Id", "alice")
    for v in values:
        conn.putheader(header, v)
    conn.endheaders()
    conn.send(raw)
    resp = conn.getresponse()
    return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())


def main():
    shutil.rmtree(ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
    audit_log = AuditLog(ROOT)
    store = KeyStore(ROOT, audit_log)
    policies = PolicyStore(ROOT, audit_log)
    coordinator = restore_mod.RestoreCoordinator(store, policies)
    operations = OperationStore(ROOT, store, policies, coordinator)
    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(
        ("127.0.0.1", PORT),
        make_handler(store, policies, coordinator, operations),
    )
    httpd.daemon_threads = True
    t = threading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    time.sleep(0.2)

    tenant = "tenant-e2e"
    # Create an AES key (non-idempotent endpoint).
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys",
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256", "label": "k"})
    check("create 201", s == 201, (s, r))
    key_id = r["key_id"]

    # --- header validation: missing / illegal / duplicate, no side effects
    events_before = count_rotate_events(tenant, key_id)
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"})
    check("missing Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400 and "error" in r
          and "operation_id" not in r, (s, r))
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": "bad key!"})
    check("illegal Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": ""})
    check("empty Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))
    s, r = http_dup_header("/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id, "Idempotency-Key",
                           ["k1", "k2"],
                           {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"})
    check("duplicate Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": "x" * 129})
    check("129-char Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))
    check("validation failures have no side effects",
          count_rotate_events(tenant, key_id) == events_before)

    # --- successful rotate + replay
    idem = "rotate-1"
    body = {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"}
    s, r1 = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id, body,
                 {"Idempotency-Key": idem})
    check("rotate 201 with operation_id",
          s == 201 and r1.get("version") == 2
          and is_uuid(r1.get("operation_id")), (s, r1))
    op_id = r1["operation_id"]
    check("success body has no extra keys",
          set(r1) == {"key_id", "version", "algorithm", "public_key",
                      "operation_id"}, sorted(r1))
    s, r2 = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id, body,
                 {"Idempotency-Key": idem})
    check("replay same binding -> same 201",
          s == 201 and r2 == r1, (r1, r2))
    s, cur = http("GET", "/v1/keys/%s/current?tenant_id=%s" % (key_id, tenant))
    check("replay did not add a version", cur["version"] == 2, cur)
    check("replay reuses one audit event",
          count_events(tenant) and
          sum(1 for e in read_events()
              if e["tenant_id"] == tenant and e["action"] == "rotate"
              and e["event_id"] == op_id) == 1)

    # --- same binding, different body -> 409 naming existing operation
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "RSA2048"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": idem})
    check("same key different body -> 409",
          s == 409 and r.get("operation_id") == op_id
          and set(r) == {"error", "operation_id"}, (s, r))
    s, cur = http("GET", "/v1/keys/%s/current?tenant_id=%s" % (key_id, tenant))
    check("409 changed nothing", cur["version"] == 2, cur)

    # --- GET operation status and tenant/operator isolation
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (op_id, tenant))
    check("GET operation 200",
          s == 200 and r["status"] == STATUS_SUCCEEDED
          and r["http_status"] == 201 and r["response"] == r1
          and r["tenant_id"] == tenant and r["operation_id"] == op_id, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=other" % op_id)
    check("cross-tenant GET -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (op_id, tenant),
                headers={"X-Operator-Id": "bob"})
    check("cross-operator GET -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s"
                % (str(uuid.uuid4()), tenant))
    check("unknown operation -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/not-a-uuid?tenant_id=%s" % tenant)
    check("malformed operation id -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s" % op_id)
    check("GET operation requires tenant -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))

    # --- policy denial is a stored 403 and replays with the same event
    from keymgr.policy import Rule
    policies.put(tenant, [Rule(subject="alice", actions=["rotate"],
                               effect="deny")])
    idem2 = "rotate-denied"
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": idem2})
    check("denied rotate -> 403 stored as failed with operation_id",
          s == 403 and set(r) == {"error", "operation_id"}, (s, r))
    deny_op = r["operation_id"]
    s, r2 = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                 {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                 {"Idempotency-Key": idem2})
    check("denied rotate replays 403", s == 403 and r2 == r, (r, r2))
    check("denial reuses one rejected event",
          sum(1 for e in read_events()
              if e["event_id"] == deny_op) == 1)
    s, st = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (deny_op, tenant))
    check("GET shows failed/403",
          st["status"] == STATUS_FAILED and st["http_status"] == 403, st)
    policies.delete(tenant)

    # --- unknown key rotate -> stored 404 (CLI exit 4), replay identical
    unknown = str(uuid.uuid4())
    idem3 = "rotate-unknown"
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % unknown,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": idem3})
    check("unknown key -> 404 + operation_id",
          s == 404 and set(r) == {"error", "operation_id"}, (s, r))
    unknown_op = r["operation_id"]
    s, r2 = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % unknown,
                 {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                 {"Idempotency-Key": idem3})
    check("unknown-key 404 replays", s == 404 and r2 == r, (r, r2))

    # --- pending record shape via GET (fabricated pending file)
    pend_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    pend = OperationRecord(
        operation_id=pend_id, idempotency_key="x", tenant_id=tenant,
        operator="alice", path="/v1/restore",
        request_fingerprint="0" * 64,
    )
    operations._persist(pend)
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (pend_id, tenant))
    check("pending GET has null http_status/response",
          s == 200 and r["status"] == STATUS_PENDING
          and r["http_status"] is None and r["response"] is None, r)
    os.unlink(operations._op_path(pend_id))

    # --- import idempotency: export then import into another tenant
    s, exp = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/export" % key_id,
                  {"tenant_id": tenant, "passphrase": "pw"})
    check("export 200", s == 200, (s, exp))
    tenant2 = "tenant-imp"
    ibody = {"tenant_id": tenant2, "passphrase": "pw", "bundle": exp["bundle"]}
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/import", ibody,
                {"Idempotency-Key": "imp-1"})
    check("import 201 + operation_id",
          s == 201 and r["key_id"] == key_id and is_uuid(r["operation_id"]),
          (s, r))
    imp_op = r["operation_id"]
    imp_resp = dict(r)
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/import", ibody,
                {"Idempotency-Key": "imp-1"})
    check("import replay identical", s == 201 and r == imp_resp, (r, imp_resp))
    # same key, tampered bundle with same binding -> 409 (binding mismatch),
    # even though the tampered bundle would independently be a 400.
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/import",
                {"tenant_id": tenant2, "passphrase": "pw",
                 "bundle": exp["bundle"][:-2] + "AA"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": "imp-1"})
    check("import same key different body -> 409",
          s == 409 and r["operation_id"] == imp_op, (s, r))
    # fresh key against same tenant -> same-tenant conflict 409 stored
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/import", ibody,
                {"Idempotency-Key": "imp-2"})
    check("same-tenant re-import -> 409 conflict",
          s == 409 and r["operation_id"] != imp_op, (s, r))
    s, st = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s"
                 % (r["operation_id"], tenant2))
    check("409 stored as conflict",
          st["status"] == STATUS_CONFLICT and st["http_status"] == 409, st)

    # --- tenant backup/restore idempotency into a fresh data dir tenant
    s, bk = http("POST", "/v1/backup",
                 {"tenant_id": tenant, "passphrase": "pw"})
    check("backup 200", s == 200, (s, bk))
    tenant3 = "tenant-rest"
    rbody = {"tenant_id": tenant3, "passphrase": "pw", "bundle": bk["bundle"]}
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/restore", rbody,
                {"Idempotency-Key": "res-1"})
    check("restore 201 + operation_id",
          s == 201 and r["tenant_id"] == tenant3
          and key_id in r["key_ids"] and is_uuid(r["operation_id"]), (s, r))
    res_resp = dict(r)
    res_op = r["operation_id"]
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/restore", rbody,
                {"Idempotency-Key": "res-1"})
    check("restore replay identical", s == 201 and r == res_resp, (r, res_resp))
    check("restore committed exactly one import event",
          sum(1 for e in read_events()
              if e["tenant_id"] == tenant3 and e["action"] == "import"
              and e["event_id"] == res_op) == 1)
    # restoring again with a different binding -> same-tenant 409
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/restore", rbody,
                {"Idempotency-Key": "res-2"})
    check("second restore -> 409", s == 409 and is_uuid(r["operation_id"]),
          (s, r))

    httpd.shutdown()

        sys.exit(1)

def read_events():
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit.log")) as fh:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in fh if line.strip()]


def count_events(tenant):
    return sum(1 for e in read_events() if e["tenant_id"] == tenant)


def count_rotate_events(tenant, key_id):
    return sum(1 for e in read_events()
               if e["tenant_id"] == tenant and e["action"] == "rotate")


def is_uuid(v):
    try:
        return uuid.UUID(v).version == 4
    except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):
        return False


def concurrency_check(operations):
    tenant = "tenant-conc"
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys",

    def slow_rotate(algorithm):
        if not state["slept"]:
            state["slept"] = True
            time.sleep(6.0)
        return orig_rotate(algorithm)

    local.rotate = slow_rotate

            key_id=key_id, payload={"tenant_id": tenant,
                                    "algorithm": "AES256"})

    t2 = threading.Thread(target=call, args=("waiter", "same"))

    t2.start()

    holder = results.get("holder")
    check("waiter timed_out 503",

        and waiter.status == "timed_out",

def cli(args):
    p = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "keymgr", "--data-dir", ROOT] + args,
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    out = p.stdout.strip()
    err = p.stderr.strip()
    return p.returncode, (json.loads(out) if out else None), (
        json.loads(err) if err else None)

                 {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},

    # ...CLI replays the same binding and body.

                      "--algorithm", "AES256", "--operator", "alice",
                      "--idempotency-key", "cli-http-1"])
    check("CLI replays HTTP operation identically",
          rc == 0 and r == hr, (rc, r, hr))
    # CLI-first then HTTP replay (import flow).
    s, bk = http("POST", "/v1/backup",
                 {"tenant_id": tenant, "passphrase": "pw"})
    rc, r, err = cli(["restore", "--tenant-id", "tenant-cli-rest",
                      "--passphrase", "pw", "--bundle", bk["bundle"],
                      "--operator", "alice",
                      "--idempotency-key", "http-cli-1"])
    check("CLI restore 0", rc == 0 and r and r["operation_id"], (rc, r, err))
    cli_op = r["operation_id"]
    s, hr2 = http("POST", "/v1/restore",
                  {"tenant_id": "tenant-cli-rest", "passphrase": "pw",
                   "bundle": bk["bundle"]},
                  {"Idempotency-Key": "http-cli-1"})
    check("HTTP replays CLI restore identically",
          s == 201 and hr2["operation_id"] == cli_op
          and hr2["key_ids"] == r["key_ids"], (s, hr2, r))
    # CLI missing idempotency key -> argparse exit 2
    rc, out, err = cli(["rotate", "--tenant-id", tenant, "--key-id", key_id,
                        "--algorithm", "AES256", "--operator", "alice"])
    check("CLI without --idempotency-key exits 2", rc == 2, (rc, err))
    # CLI illegal key -> exit 2, stderr error only
    rc, out, err = cli(["rotate", "--tenant-id", tenant, "--key-id", key_id,
                        "--algorithm", "AES256", "--operator", "alice",
                        "--idempotency-key", "bad key"])
    check("CLI illegal key exits 2", rc == 2 and "error" in err, (rc, err))
    # CLI same key different body -> exit 3 with existing operation_id
    rc, out, err = cli(["rotate", "--tenant-id", tenant, "--key-id", key_id,
                        "--algorithm", "RSA2048", "--operator", "alice",
                        "--idempotency-key", "cli-http-1"])
    check("CLI binding conflict exits 3",
          rc == 3 and err.get("operation_id") == cli_op
          or (rc == 3 and err and err.get("operation_id")), (rc, err))


def crash_recovery_checks():
    """A pending op whose event committed is finalized on restart."""
    data_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, "crash")
    os.makedirs(data_dir, exist_ok=True)
    audit_log = AuditLog(data_dir)
    store = KeyStore(data_dir, audit_log)
    policies = PolicyStore(data_dir, audit_log)

    op_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

    version = rotated.current.version

    # Rebuild a fresh process: key/policy/restore recovery runs, then the

    store2 = KeyStore(data_dir, AuditLog(data_dir))
    policies2 = PolicyStore(data_dir, AuditLog(data_dir))
    coord2 = restore_mod.RestoreCoordinator(store2, policies2)

          got is not None and got.status == STATUS_SUCCEEDED

          and got.response["operation_id"] == op_id, got)
    # A pending op with NO event stays pending; a same-binding live retry
    # re-executes it under the same operation_id and commits.
    op2 = str(uuid.uuid4())
    pend2 = OperationRecord(
        operation_id=op2, idempotency_key="crash-2",
        tenant_id="tenant-crash", operator="alice",
        path="/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
        request_fingerprint=ops_mod.canonical_fingerprint(
            "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
            {"tenant_id": "tenant-crash", "algorithm": "AES256"}),
        intent={"kind": "rotate", "key_id": key_id},
    )
    ops2._persist(pend2)
    ops3 = OperationStore(data_dir, store2, policies2, coord2)
    still = ops3.get_operation(op2, "tenant-crash", "alice")
    check("crash: uncommitted pending op stays pending",
          still is not None and still.status == STATUS_PENDING, still)

        idempotency_key="crash-2", key_id=key_id,
        payload={"tenant_id": "tenant-crash", "algorithm": "AES256"})
    check("crash: live retry under same op id commits",
          rec2.operation_id == op2 and rec2.http_status == 201, rec2)

"""End-to-end checks for idempotent rotate/import/restore."""

from keymgr.audit import AuditLog

    OperationStore, OperationRecord, STATUS_SUCCEEDED, STATUS_FAILED,
    STATUS_CONFLICT, STATUS_PENDING,
)

from keymgr import restore as restore_mod
from keymgr.server import make_handler
from keymgr.store import KeyStore
from keymgr.crypto import SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS

ROOT = "/tmp/keymgr_idem_test"
PORT = 18099

failures = []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    if cond:
        print("PASS", name)
    else:
        print("FAIL", name, detail)
        failures.append(name)


def http(method, path, body=None, headers=None, raw=None):
    url = "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (PORT, path)
    data = raw if raw is not None else (
        json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    )
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
    req.add_header("X-Operator-Id", "alice")
    for k, v in (headers or {}).items():
        if k.lower() == "x-operator-id":
            req.remove_header("X-Operator-Id") if False else None
        req.add_header(k, v)
    # urllib dedups headers by combining; to truly duplicate a header use low-level
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, json.loads(e.read())


def http_dup_header(path, header, values, body):
    """Send a request with a genuinely duplicated header via raw socket."""
    import http.client
    conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", PORT, timeout=10)
    conn.putrequest("POST", path)
    conn.putheader("Content-Type", "application/json")
    raw = json.dumps(body).encode()
    conn.putheader("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
    conn.putheader("X-Operator-Id", "alice")
    for v in values:
        conn.putheader(header, v)
    conn.endheaders()
    conn.send(raw)
    resp = conn.getresponse()
    return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())


def main():
    shutil.rmtree(ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
    audit_log = AuditLog(ROOT)
    store = KeyStore(ROOT, audit_log)
    policies = PolicyStore(ROOT, audit_log)
    coordinator = restore_mod.RestoreCoordinator(store, policies)
    operations = OperationStore(ROOT, store, policies, coordinator)
    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(
        ("127.0.0.1", PORT),
        make_handler(store, policies, coordinator, operations),
    )
    httpd.daemon_threads = True
    t = threading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    time.sleep(0.2)

    tenant = "tenant-e2e"
    # Create an AES key (non-idempotent endpoint).
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys",
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256", "label": "k"})
    check("create 201", s == 201, (s, r))
    key_id = r["key_id"]

    # --- header validation: missing / illegal / duplicate, no side effects
    events_before = count_rotate_events(tenant, key_id)
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"})
    check("missing Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400 and "error" in r
          and "operation_id" not in r, (s, r))
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": "bad key!"})
    check("illegal Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,

    s, r = http_dup_header("/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id, "Idempotency-Key",
                           ["k1", "k2"],

    check("duplicate Idempotency-Key -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))

                {"Idempotency-Key": "x" * 129})

    check("validation failures have no side effects",
          count_rotate_events(tenant, key_id) == events_before)

    idem = "rotate-1"
    body = {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"}

                 {"Idempotency-Key": idem})
    check("rotate 201 with operation_id",

    s, cur = http("GET", "/v1/keys/%s/current?tenant_id=%s" % (key_id, tenant))
    check("replay did not add a version", cur["version"] == 2, cur)
    check("replay reuses one audit event",
          count_events(tenant) and
          sum(1 for e in read_events()

                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "RSA2048"},

          s == 409 and r.get("operation_id") == op_id

    s, cur = http("GET", "/v1/keys/%s/current?tenant_id=%s" % (key_id, tenant))
    check("409 changed nothing", cur["version"] == 2, cur)

    # --- GET operation status and tenant/operator isolation
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (op_id, tenant))

          s == 200 and r["status"] == STATUS_SUCCEEDED
          and r["http_status"] == 201 and r["response"] == r1
          and r["tenant_id"] == tenant and r["operation_id"] == op_id, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=other" % op_id)
    check("cross-tenant GET -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (op_id, tenant),
                headers={"X-Operator-Id": "bob"})
    check("cross-operator GET -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s"
                % (str(uuid.uuid4()), tenant))
    check("unknown operation -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/not-a-uuid?tenant_id=%s" % tenant)
    check("malformed operation id -> 404", s == 404, (s, r))
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s" % op_id)
    check("GET operation requires tenant -> 400", s == 400, (s, r))

    from keymgr.policy import Rule
    policies.put(tenant, [Rule(subject="alice", actions=["rotate"],

    idem2 = "rotate-denied"
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": idem2})
    check("denied rotate -> 403 stored as failed with operation_id",
          s == 403 and set(r) == {"error", "operation_id"}, (s, r))
    deny_op = r["operation_id"]
    s, r2 = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
                 {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                 {"Idempotency-Key": idem2})
    check("denied rotate replays 403", s == 403 and r2 == r, (r, r2))
    check("denial reuses one rejected event",
          sum(1 for e in read_events()

    s, st = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (deny_op, tenant))

                {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                {"Idempotency-Key": idem3})
    check("unknown key -> 404 + operation_id",
          s == 404 and set(r) == {"error", "operation_id"}, (s, r))
    unknown_op = r["operation_id"]

                 {"tenant_id": tenant, "algorithm": "AES256"},
                 {"Idempotency-Key": idem3})
    check("unknown-key 404 replays", s == 404 and r2 == r, (r, r2))

    # --- pending record shape via GET (fabricated pending file)
    pend_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    pend = OperationRecord(
        operation_id=pend_id, idempotency_key="x", tenant_id=tenant,
        operator="alice", path="/v1/restore",
        request_fingerprint="0" * 64,
    )
    operations._persist(pend)
    s, r = http("GET", "/v1/operations/%s?tenant_id=%s" % (pend_id, tenant))

          s == 200 and r["status"] == STATUS_PENDING
          and r["http_status"] is None and r["response"] is None, r)
    os.unlink(operations._op_path(pend_id))

    # --- import idempotency: export then import into another tenant
    s, exp = http("POST", "/v1/keys/%s/export" % key_id,
                  {"tenant_id": tenant, "passphrase": "pw"})
    check("export 200", s == 200, (s, exp))
    tenant2 = "tenant-imp"

          s == 201 and r["key_id"] == key_id and is_uuid(r["operation_id"]),

    imp_op = r["operation_id"]

    res_op = r["operation_id"]
    s, r = http("POST", "/v1/restore", rbody,
                {"Idempotency-Key": "res-1"})

    check("restore committed exactly one import event",
          sum(1 for e in read_events()

                {"tenant_id": "tenant-empty", "passphrase": "pw",

def read_events():
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit.log")) as fh:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in fh if line.strip()]


def count_events(tenant):
    return sum(1 for e in read_events() if e["tenant_id"] == tenant)


def count_rotate_events(tenant, key_id):
    return sum(1 for e in read_events()
               if e["tenant_id"] == tenant and e["action"] == "rotate")


def is_uuid(v):
    try:

    except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):

def concurrency_check(operations):
    tenant = "tenant-conc"

            tenant_id=tenant, operator="alice", idempotency_key=key,

def crash_recovery_checks():
    """A pending op whose event committed is finalized on restart."""
    data_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, "crash")
    os.makedirs(data_dir, exist_ok=True)
    audit_log = AuditLog(data_dir)
    store = KeyStore(data_dir, audit_log)
    policies = PolicyStore(data_dir, audit_log)
    coordinator = restore_mod.RestoreCoordinator(store, policies)
    rec = store.create("tenant-crash", "AES256", "k")
    key_id = rec.key_id
    op_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    # Simulate: rotate committed outbox (event op_id in ledger), but the
    # operation record is still pending when the process died.
    rotated = store.rotate(key_id, "tenant-crash", "AES256", event_id=op_id)
    version = rotated.current.version
    operations = OperationStore(data_dir, store, policies, coordinator)
    pend = OperationRecord(
        operation_id=op_id, idempotency_key="crash-1",
        tenant_id="tenant-crash", operator="alice",
        path="/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
        request_fingerprint="0" * 64,
        intent={"kind": "rotate", "key_id": key_id},
    )
    operations._persist(pend)
    # Rebuild a fresh process: key/policy/restore recovery runs, then the
    # operation store finalizes the pending record from the ledger.
    store2 = KeyStore(data_dir, AuditLog(data_dir))
    policies2 = PolicyStore(data_dir, AuditLog(data_dir))
    coord2 = restore_mod.RestoreCoordinator(store2, policies2)
    ops2 = OperationStore(data_dir, store2, policies2, coord2)
    got = ops2.get_operation(op_id, "tenant-crash", "alice")
    check("crash: committed pending op finalized succeeded",
          got is not None and got.status == STATUS_SUCCEEDED
          and got.http_status == 201 and got.response["version"] == version
          and got.response["operation_id"] == op_id, got)
    # A pending op with NO event stays pending; a same-binding live retry
    # re-executes it under the same operation_id and commits.
    op2 = str(uuid.uuid4())
    pend2 = OperationRecord(
        operation_id=op2, idempotency_key="crash-2",
        tenant_id="tenant-crash", operator="alice",
        path="/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
        request_fingerprint=ops_mod.canonical_fingerprint(
            "/v1/keys/%s/rotate" % key_id,
            {"tenant_id": "tenant-crash", "algorithm": "AES256"}),
        intent={"kind": "rotate", "key_id": key_id},
    )
    ops2._persist(pend2)
    ops3 = OperationStore(data_dir, store2, policies2, coord2)
    still = ops3.get_operation(op2, "tenant-crash", "alice")
    check("crash: uncommitted pending op stays pending",
          still is not None and still.status == STATUS_PENDING, still)
    rec2 = ops3.run_rotate(
        tenant_id="tenant-crash", operator="alice",
        idempotency_key="crash-2", key_id=key_id,
        payload={"tenant_id": "tenant-crash", "algorithm": "AES256"})
    check("crash: live retry under same op id commits",
          rec2.operation_id == op2 and rec2.http_status == 201, rec2)
